definition.interpretation: The initial evaluation of memory-augmented agents shows a divergence rate (0.066) that satisfies the hypothesis prediction (>= 0.05). This suggests that memory-augmented architectures may indeed exhibit path-dependent behaviors distinguishable from standard Markovian agents, though the synthetic method requires validation with more complex environment configurations.
definition.limitations: The use of a mock Python-based environment limits the generalizability of the divergence measurements. Independent validation and comparison against non-memory-augmented baselines are necessary to isolate the effect of memory from random noise.
definition.next_step: Refine the experimental protocol to include a control group (standard RL) and execute a comparative study.
